title: Bitwise file permissions
instructorPromptText: Write a C program that simulates UNIX-style file permissions (Read=4, Write=2, Execute=1) using bitwise flags. Implement functions to add a permission, remove a permission, and check if a permission is set using bitwise operators (`|`, `&`, `~`).

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program correctly use bitwise OR (`|`) to add/grant permissions without affecting other flags?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Using `|` ensures that adding an already existing permission is idempotent, whereas arithmetic `+` would corrupt the bitmask.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program correctly use bitwise AND with NOT (`& ~`) to remove/revoke permissions?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Revoking a permission requires masking with the inverse flag; using arithmetic `-` would fail if the permission was not already set.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program use bitwise AND (`&`) to check if a specific permission bit is set?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Verifies that checking permissions isolates the target bit rather than checking if any permission is set.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student uses arithmetic addition `+` to add a permission or subtraction `-` to remove it.
Student uses logical operators (`||`, `&&`, `!`) instead of bitwise ones (`|`, `&`, `~`).
Student defines permissions using an `enum` or `#define` macros (e.g. `READ = 4`) rather than raw magic numbers.
Student uses different function names or parameters than the ones committed in their specification.
Student writes the removal operation as `n = n & ~mask` but gets the operator precedence wrong or forgets the bitwise NOT.
